parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure Node.js ESM modules in /output, exact argparse behavior, bytes repr, construct integer and bytes behavior, no external imports, and no prohibited DataView or ArrayBuffer interface.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept implementation ownership while a workflow owned behavioral characterization with four probe children and a critic phase; the int-parsing probe stalled and was retried.
parallel.implementation: Parent wrote a broad module hierarchy for unicode digits, whitespace, printable handling, python int/bytes/repr, construct fields/errors, argparse parser/formatter, runtime traceback, app main, entrypoint, and diff tools.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The copied artifact contained test19.mjs, tools, and multiple lib modules; no child implemented competing components, but the workflow never returned a consolidated critic result before kill.
parallel.verification: Parent ran sample tests and began differential testing; the larger diff run first timed out and then crashed on a NUL argv case, leaving verification unfinished at the visible end of the parent trajectory.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 1 of 30; the parent process timed out with no final response and the characterization workflow was killed with the int-parsing retry still active.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, exact argv, formatting, zero-dependency, hierarchical module, black-box probing, and /output placement requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, integration, bug fixing, and verification end to end without delegation or child handoffs.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote equivalent local modules for bytes, strings, int parsing, argparse formatting/parser, construct errors/fields, traceback rendering, and test19.mjs, then refined them from diff failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial artifact included the entrypoint and library hierarchy and the final response summarized the delivered files and behavior coverage.
serial.verification: Serial ran sample cases, a 56-case differential suite from two cwd states, help and usage width sweeps, and fuzz batches with zero observed mismatches after fixes.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 1 of 30 despite normal process completion; the available summary does not identify the remaining failing hidden case.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official status evaluations completed and both marked solution_passed false with 29 of 30 samples passed, so the official outcome relation is both_fail rather than a discordant split. The main comparative difference is process: parallel lost time and closure to a checkpoint-free retry inside a killed characterization workflow, while serial completed local verification and final reporting. The available evaluator summaries do not expose the identity of the one failed hidden sample, so the retained coordination pattern is an adverse parallel process difference, not a proven explanation for a pass/fail divergence.
parallel_contributors: Workflow-based characterization left the int-parsing retry unfinished and the parent timed out with an empty final response.
Parallel verification was still recovering from a crashed differential harness around a NUL argv case at the last visible parent action.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all probing, implementation, and fixes in one trajectory and reached normal final response.
Serial reran differential and fuzz checks from multiple cwd states after fixing argparse help and wrapping behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both implementations still missed one official evaluator sample; the pair evidence does not identify the remaining hidden edge case.
evaluator_effects: The visible official summaries provide only aggregate 29/30 results, not the failing testcase details.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no discordant outcome; supported process contrast, not an exclusive root cause
